clue.text: Expression of masculinity, measure of speed shown by one's doctor

parts.note: a Mach number measures speed relative to the speed of sound
one is I, and the 's adds S, as in I'S
MO is a medical officer, an army doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor's speedometer reading somehow counts as a display of manliness.
explanation.definitionFit: Machismo is a strong, often exaggerated, show of manliness and toughness.

clue.text: Device in Palace re-designed to restrict parking

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so the rearranged letters close around the parking letter
something re-designed is laid out anew, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: P is the standard road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A gadget installed in a palace makeover limits where cars may park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is part of the fodder, not a link: the letters of IN PALACE are rearranged around P.
explanation.definitionFit: An appliance is a machine or tool for a household task, a kind of device.

clue.text: Holiday location turning up in epistle to home

indicators.note: turning up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A holiday spot crops up in a letter written back home.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside 'epistle to home' and, this being a down clue, 'turning up' reads them from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel is where many people stay on holiday, so it is a fair example of a holiday location.

clue.text: Energy required to hold high note, just for a while

indicators.note: to hold is to contain, so the energy word wraps around the next pieces

parts.note: sap means vigour or vital energy
top means highest, uppermost
G is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A singer needs energy to sustain a high note, if only briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopgap is a temporary measure, used only until something better is found.

clue.text: River creature's more than enough on English river

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means excessive
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Some river animal is overdoing things on an English river.
explanation.definitionFit: The otter is a mammal that lives and hunts fish in rivers.

clue.text: UK seaway with one-third reduction in fish

indicators.note: cutting a third of a six-letter word drops two letters, here its last two

parts.note: the Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight and mainland England

explanation.surface: A British shipping channel loses a third of its fish stocks.
explanation.walkthrough: The SOLENT is the strait separating the Isle of Wight from Hampshire on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The sole is a flatfish, prized as food.

clue.text: Drink's fixed, incorporating mint?

indicators.note: incorporating means taking in, so the word for fixed wraps around the plant

parts.note: set means fixed or settled
mint is an example of a herb

explanation.surface: A drink is settled and has mint in it, like a julep.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', a link; the question mark flags mint as an example of the category.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherbet is a sweet fruit drink, or in Britain the fizzy powder used to make one.

clue.text: Meadow mostly unproductive

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: lean, as in lean years, means unproductive or meagre

explanation.surface: A field that yields little hay.
explanation.definitionFit: A lea is a poetic word for a grassy field or pasture.

clue.text: Observe maximum returns

indicators.note: returns means comes back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: tops means at the most, the maximum

explanation.surface: Watch for the highest yields on an investment.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot is to notice or catch sight of, synonymous with observe.

clue.text: Escaping no Hamlet broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A TV schedule note says Hamlet won't be shown after all.
explanation.definitionFit: On the lam is American slang for fleeing, especially from the police.

clue.text: Small-town resident gets endless dreadful beer

indicators.note: endless means without its last letter

parts.note: vile means dreadful, horrible
lager is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A local is served an unending supply of awful beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A villager lives in a village, a small rural settlement.

clue.text: Point, indicating second stop on pub crawl

parts.note: a pub crawl goes from bar to bar
B is the second letter, as in plan B

explanation.surface: Someone notes the second pub visited on a night out.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Bar B' as a label for the second stop.
explanation.definitionFit: A barb is a sharp backward-pointing tip, as on a fish-hook or arrow.

clue.text: Artist using eye movement to mark conclusion of portrait

parts.note: REM is rapid eye movement, the dreaming phase of sleep
to brand is to mark, as with a hot iron

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A painter uses the viewer's gaze to finish off a portrait.
explanation.definitionFit: Rembrandt was the great seventeenth-century Dutch painter, famed for portraits.

clue.text: Ace menu option, designed for a fairy tale start?

indicators.note: designed means planned or put together, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A restaurant devises a great dish for a fairy-tale opening.
explanation.definitionFit: Traditional fairy stories open with this stock phrase, so it is their customary first words.

clue.text: Easily moved by name of delightful spot

indicators.note: moved means shifted around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A beautiful place is effortlessly changed by its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Elysian describes Elysium, the paradise of Greek myth, so it means belonging to a blissful place.

clue.text: Developing article that's picked up trail

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a scent is the trail an animal leaves for hounds to follow

explanation.surface: A news piece in progress has found a lead to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent means just coming into being and beginning to grow.

clue.text: Tax: it's not involved in light-heartedness

indicators.note: not involved in means kept out of, so those letters are removed from inside

parts.note: levity means frivolity or light-heartedness
the word it, with 's for is acting as a link

explanation.surface: Taxation is no laughing matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A levy is a charge or duty imposed by authority, a form of tax.

clue.text: Dangerous blaze: vehicle with lease taken round front of farm

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle

indicators.note: taken round means wrapped around, so the rental word encloses the farm letter

parts.note: to hire is to lease or rent

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A rented coach drives around a farm while a wildfire rages.
explanation.definitionFit: A bushfire is a wildfire in scrub or forest, a term common in Australia.

clue.text: Prohibit a line in stock

parts.note: to ban is to prohibit

explanation.surface: An order to stop a product line being held in a warehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock, as in a stock phrase, means trite or commonplace.

clue.text: Illness Father catches the day before

indicators.note: catches means grabs hold of, so the priest's title encloses the next piece

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
eve is the day before a festival, as in Christmas Eve

explanation.surface: A priest picks up a bug the day before an event.
explanation.definitionFit: A fever is a raised body temperature, and loosely an illness marked by one.

clue.text: Confrontation of French by groom-to-be

parts.note: de is French for of
a fiancé is a man engaged to be married

explanation.surface: A French bridegroom faces a showdown.
explanation.definitionFit: Defiance is open resistance, a bold confronting of authority.

clue.text: Spy, upset, dumping nothing in tree

indicators.note: dumping means discarding, so a letter is removed
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation
O, the zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: An agitated secret agent throws something away while hiding in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns MOLE into ELOM, and 'dumping' then loses its O.
explanation.definitionFit: The elm is a large deciduous tree.

clue.text: Artist abandoning chasm to depict plant

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: a ravine is a deep narrow gorge, a chasm
RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A painter leaves a gorge to paint some greenery.
explanation.definitionFit: A vine is a climbing plant, especially the grapevine.

clue.text: Congregation's response put right without end

indicators.note: without end means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to amend is to correct or put right

explanation.surface: Worshippers reply to a correction that never finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Worshippers say this word in unison at the end of a prayer to affirm it.

clue.text: Channel's latest repeat exhibiting culture?

indicators.note: the latest part of a word is its final letter

parts.note: to iterate is to repeat

explanation.surface: A TV station's newest rerun shows off its highbrow side.
explanation.definitionFit: Being literate means educated and well-read, which is one sign of a cultured person.
